alg-discrete-l-curve-parameter-choice:
## Definition

Input a real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, data $b\in\mathbb R^m$,
and a strictly increasing finite grid $0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_q$ with
$q\ge3$. For each grid point, compute the unique Tikhonov minimizer
$$x_j=(A^TA+\lambda_j I)^{-1}A^Tb,$$
and the residual $r_j=\|Ax_j-b\|$ and solution norm $s_j=\|x_j\|$.
Discard any index with $r_j=0$ or $s_j=0$. If fewer than three indices
remain, return failure status `insufficient-valid-points`.

For consecutive retained indices $i_0<i_1<i_2$, set
$p_k=(\log r_{i_k},\log s_{i_k})\in\mathbb R^2$, $u=p_1-p_0$,
and $v=p_2-p_1$. Define their discrete curvature by
$$\kappa=\begin{cases} \dfrac{2|\det(u,v)|}{\|u\|\,\|v\|\,\|u+v\|},&\|u\|\,\|v\|\,\|u+v\|>0,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$
Assign this curvature to the middle retained index. Among the resulting
$q'-2$ values, return the original grid parameter whose curvature is largest;
if there is a tie, return the tied parameter with the smallest original index.
No uniform-grid spacing is assumed in log parameter. This is a finite-grid
heuristic and carries no universal optimality claim.

The output is either a selected $\lambda_j$ with its discrete curvature and
index, or the stated failure status. Every step uses a finite loop over the
input grid.
lem-compact-gram-operator-is-positive-an:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces and let
$A:X\to Y$ be compact and bounded, with adjoint $A^*:Y\to X$. Then both
$A^*A:X\to X$ and $AA^*:Y\to Y$ are compact, self-adjoint and positive, and
$$\ker(A^*A)=\ker A,\qquad \ker(AA^*)=\ker A^*.$$
lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
$H$ be an $\mathbb F$-Hilbert space, and let $S:H\to H$ be compact and
self-adjoint. Let $\Sigma$ be its set of nonzero
eigenvalues, $E_t=\ker(S-tI)$, $P_t$ the orthogonal projection onto $E_t$,
and $P_0$ the orthogonal projection onto $\ker S$. If
$q:\{0\}\cup\Sigma\to\mathbb F$ is bounded, then for every $x\in H$ the
finite-subset net
$$q(0)P_0x+\sum_{t\in F}q(t)P_tx,\qquad F\subseteq\Sigma\text{ finite},$$
converges in norm to a vector $Q_qx$. The map $Q_q:H\to H$ is bounded and
linear, with $\|Q_q\|\le\sup_{t\in\{0\}\cup\Sigma}|q(t)|$.
lem-linear-smoother-gcv-expression:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge1$, let $b\in\mathbb R^m$,
and let $\lambda>0$. Define
$$x_\lambda=(A^TA+\lambda I)^{-1}A^Tb,\qquad H_\lambda=A(A^TA+\lambda I)^{-1}A^T,$$
so the fitted vector is $H_\lambda b$. For row $a_i^T$ of $A$, let
$x_\lambda^{(-i)}$ be the same Tikhonov minimizer after deleting row $i$ and
entry $b_i$. Then $1-(H_\lambda)_{ii}>0$ and
$$b_i-a_i^Tx_\lambda^{(-i)}=\frac{((I-H_\lambda)b)_i}{1-(H_\lambda)_{ii}}.$$
Consequently exact leave-one-out squared prediction error is
$$\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\frac{((I-H_\lambda)b)_i}{1-(H_\lambda)_{ii}}\right)^2.$$
Replacing every diagonal leverage $(H_\lambda)_{ii}$ in this expression by
their mean $\operatorname{tr}(H_\lambda)/m$ gives the GCV score
$$\operatorname{GCV}(\lambda)=\frac{\|(I-H_\lambda)b\|^2}{m\bigl(1-\operatorname{tr}(H_\lambda)/m\bigr)^2}.$$
This trace-average replacement is the GCV approximation; it is not an exact
identity for leave-one-out error unless the diagonal entries are equal.
lem-square-summable-sequences-form-a-hil:
## Statement

The real sequence space
$$\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)=\left\{x=(x_n):\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|x_n|^2<\infty\right\},$$
with its canonical inner product and norm from
[[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]], is complete and
therefore is a real Hilbert space.
alg-gcv-finite-grid-parameter-choice:
## Definition

Input a real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge1$, data
$b\in\mathbb R^m$, and a nonempty strictly increasing finite grid
$0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_N$. For each $\lambda_j$, compute the unique
Tikhonov minimizer $x_j=(A^TA+\lambda_j I)^{-1}A^Tb$, form
$H_j=A(A^TA+\lambda_j I)^{-1}A^T$, and compute
$$G_j=\frac{\|(I-H_j)b\|^2} {m\bigl(1-\operatorname{tr}(H_j)/m\bigr)^2}.$$
The denominator is positive because $\lambda_j>0$ makes every eigenvalue of
$H_j$ strictly less than one. Return the pair $(\lambda_j,G_j)$ with minimal
score; if several grid points minimize it, return the smallest index. Also
return the full finite list of scores. This rule minimizes the stated GCV
score on its supplied grid; it does not claim to minimize the unknown solution
error or to be universally optimal.
def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualific:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces and let
$A:X\to Y$ be compact and bounded. Put $S=A^*A$. By
[[lem-compact-gram-operator-is-positive-and-has-kernel]], $S$ is compact,
positive, and self-adjoint, with $\ker S=\ker A$. Let $\Sigma$ be the set of
nonzero eigenvalues of $S$ and $P_t$ the orthogonal projection onto the
eigenspace of $t\in\Sigma$; let $P_0$ be the orthogonal projection onto
$\ker S$. The compact spectral multiplier of a bounded scalar function
$q:\{0\}\cup\Sigma\to\mathbb F$ is
$$q(S)x:=q(0)P_0x+\sum_{t\in\Sigma}q(t)P_tx,$$
where the finite-subset net converges in norm by
[[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]]. For $\nu>0$, define
$S^\nu$ by the multiplier $q_\nu(0)=0$ and $q_\nu(t)=t^\nu$ for $t>0$.

For $\lambda>0$, the Tikhonov filter and residual filter are
$$g_\lambda(t)=\frac1{t+\lambda},\qquad r_\lambda(t)=1-tg_\lambda(t)=\frac{\lambda}{t+\lambda}.$$
The Tikhonov solution for data $y_\delta\in Y$ is
$$x_\lambda^\delta=g_\lambda(S)A^*y_\delta =(A^*A+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*y_\delta.$$
The source condition of order $\nu>0$ and radius $R\ge0$ means that
$x^\dagger=S^\nu w$ for some $w\in X$ with $\|w\|\le R$. A family of
filters $g_\alpha$ with residual filters $r_\alpha(t)=1-tg_\alpha(t)$ has
qualification at least $p>0$ when, for each $0<\nu\le p$, some finite
constant $C_\nu$ satisfies
$$\sup_{t\in\Sigma}t^\nu|r_\alpha(t)|\le C_\nu\alpha^\nu \quad\text{for every }\alpha>0.$$
thm-discrete-l-curve-grid-search-is-well:
## Statement

For every admissible finite input to
[[alg-discrete-l-curve-parameter-choice]], the algorithm terminates. It returns
failure exactly when fewer than three positive-residual, positive-solution-norm
grid points remain. Otherwise it returns a retained grid parameter whose
assigned discrete curvature is maximal; ties are resolved by the least original
grid index.
lem-tikhonov-bias-converges-for-minimum-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex
Hilbert spaces, let $x^\dagger\perp\ker A$, and put $y=Ax^\dagger$. For
$\lambda>0$, let $x_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*y$. Then
$$x^\dagger-x_\lambda=\sum_{t\in\Sigma}\frac{\lambda}{t+\lambda}P_tx^\dagger,$$
where $\Sigma$ and $P_t$ are the nonzero eigenvalues and eigenspace
projections of $A^*A$, and
$$\lim_{\lambda\downarrow0}\|x^\dagger-x_\lambda\|=0.$$
lem-tikhonov-data-residual-continuity-mo:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex
Hilbert spaces. For data $g\in Y$ and $\lambda>0$, let
$x_\lambda(g)=(A^*A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^*g$ and
$r_g(\lambda)=\|Ax_\lambda(g)-g\|$. Then $r_g$ is continuous and
nondecreasing on $(0,\infty)$, and
$$g-Ax_\lambda(g)=\lambda(AA^*+\lambda I_Y)^{-1}g, \qquad\|\lambda(AA^*+\lambda I_Y)^{-1}\|\le1,$$
and
$$\lim_{\lambda\downarrow0}r_g(\lambda) =\operatorname{dist}(g,\overline{\operatorname{Ran}A}),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}r_g(\lambda)=\|g\|.$$
lem-tikhonov-source-condition-bias-bound:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex
Hilbert spaces, put $S=A^*A$, and suppose
$x^\dagger=S^\nu w$ with $0<\nu\le1$ and $\|w\|\le R$. Then for every
$\lambda>0$ the exact-data Tikhonov bias satisfies
$$\|x^\dagger-(A^*A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^*Ax^\dagger\| \le R\lambda^\nu.$$
Equivalently, the Tikhonov residual filter has qualification at least one in
the convention of [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]].
thm-gcv-grid-search-returns-score-minimi:
## Statement

For every admissible input to [[alg-gcv-finite-grid-parameter-choice]], all
GCV scores are finite real numbers, the algorithm terminates, and its output
has the least score on the supplied grid, with ties resolved by the least
index. This is a score-minimization statement only; it gives no bound on
solution error or universal statistical optimality.
alg-morozov-discrepancy-bracketing-and-b:
## Definition

Input a compact operator $A:X\to Y$ between real or complex Hilbert spaces,
data $g\in Y$, a declared noise level $\delta>0$, a discrepancy factor
$\tau>1$, an initial parameter $\lambda_0>0$, integer budgets $M,N\ge0$,
and an exact residual evaluator for
$$r_g(\lambda)=\|A(A^*A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^*g-g\|.$$
The admissible endpoint condition is
$$d:=\operatorname{dist}(g,\overline{\operatorname{Ran}A}) <\tau\delta<\|g\|.$$
The endpoint values $d$ and $\|g\|$ are supplied as exact certified inputs;
the algorithm does not infer an infinite-dimensional range distance from a
finite number of residual evaluations. If the supplied values fail
$d<\tau\delta<\|g\|$, return `incompatible-endpoints`.

Set $q=\tau\delta$ and evaluate $r_g(\lambda_0)$. If it is below $q$, set
$\lambda_-=\lambda_0$ and repeatedly double the upper endpoint, at most $M$
times, until $r_g(\lambda_+)\ge q$. If the initial residual is at least $q$,
set $\lambda_+=\lambda_0$ and repeatedly halve the lower endpoint, at most
$M$ times, until $r_g(\lambda_-)<q$. If either search exhausts its budget
without a bracket, return `budget-exhausted`; this status is inconclusive.

With a bracket satisfying $r_g(\lambda_-)<q\le r_g(\lambda_+)$, repeat
$N$ times: set $\lambda_m=(\lambda_-+\lambda_+)/2$; if $r_g(\lambda_m)<q$,
replace $\lambda_-$ by $\lambda_m$, and otherwise replace $\lambda_+$ by
$\lambda_m$. Return the bracket $[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]$. Continuity and
monotonicity imply that it contains the first exact Morozov crossing. The
algorithm returns a bracket, not a universal accuracy guarantee for a finite
budget.
thm-tikhonov-convergence-under-noise-par:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex
Hilbert spaces, $x^\dagger\perp\ker A$, and $y=Ax^\dagger$. For a sequence
$\delta_j\ge0$, data $y_j=y+e_j$ with $\|e_j\|\le\delta_j$, and parameters
$\lambda_j>0$, suppose
$$\lambda_j\to0,\qquad \frac{\delta_j}{\sqrt{\lambda_j}}\to0.$$
Then the Tikhonov solutions
$$x_j=(A^*A+\lambda_j I)^{-1}A^*y_j$$
converge in norm to $x^\dagger$. No source condition on $x^\dagger$ is
required.
thm-tikhonov-source-condition-rate-and-q:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex
Hilbert spaces and let $x^\dagger=S^\nu w$ with $S=A^*A$,
$0<\nu\le1$, and $\|w\|\le R$. For data $y_\delta=Ax^\dagger+e$ with
$\|e\|\le\delta$, the Tikhonov solution satisfies, for every $\lambda>0$,
$$\|x_\lambda^\delta-x^\dagger\| \le R\lambda^\nu+\frac{\delta}{2\sqrt\lambda}.$$
For $R,\delta>0$, choosing
$$\lambda=(\delta/R)^{2/(2\nu+1)}$$
gives
$$\|x_\lambda^\delta-x^\dagger\| \le\frac32 R^{1/(2\nu+1)}\delta^{2\nu/(2\nu+1)}.$$
The qualification cannot exceed one uniformly over compact operators: for
every $\nu>1$ there is a compact injective diagonal operator and a unit source
vector for which the bias is not $O(\lambda^\nu)$.
thm-morozov-discrepancy-choice-converges:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact between real or complex
Hilbert spaces, let $x^\dagger\perp\ker A$, and let the exact datum
$y=Ax^\dagger$ be nonzero. Fix $\tau>1$. For any sequence
$\delta_j>0$ tending to zero and data $y_j=y+e_j$ with $\|e_j\|\le\delta_j$,
assume $\tau\delta_j<\|y_j\|$ (which holds for all sufficiently large $j$
when $y\ne0$). Then for each such $j$ there exists a positive parameter
$\lambda_j$ satisfying the Morozov equation
$$\|A(A^*A+\lambda_j I)^{-1}A^*y_j-y_j\|=\tau\delta_j.$$
Every sequence of exact roots $\lambda_j$ of these equations satisfies
$\lambda_j\to0$, $\delta_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j}\to0$, and
$$\|(A^*A+\lambda_j I)^{-1}A^*y_j-x^\dagger\|\to0.$$
Whenever [[alg-morozov-discrepancy-bracketing-and-bisection]] returns a
bracket for the same data and target, the bracket contains at least one such
exact root. Finite-budget exhaustion remains inconclusive.
thm-tikhonov-forward-discretization-and-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be compact and $A_h:X\to Y$ be
bounded and finite rank, between real or complex Hilbert spaces. Suppose
$x^\dagger\perp\ker A$, $y=Ax^\dagger$, $y_\delta=y+e$ with
$\|e\|\le\delta$, and $\|A-A_h\|\le\eta$. Form the discretized datum
$y_{h,\delta}=A_hx^\dagger+e$ before inversion. For $\lambda>0$, define
$$R_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^*,\qquad R_{\lambda,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I)^{-1}A_h^*,$$
and for a computed output $\widetilde x_h$ define its exact normal-equation
residual
$$r_{h,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I)\widetilde x_h-A_h^*y_{h,\delta}.$$
Then
$$\begin{aligned} \|x^\dagger-\widetilde x_h\|\le{}& \|x^\dagger-R_\lambda y\| +\frac{\delta+\eta\|x^\dagger\|}{2\sqrt\lambda} +\|(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_{h,\delta}\| +\frac{\|r_{h,h}\|}{\lambda}. \end{aligned}$$
The forward-model term $\eta\|x^\dagger\|$ is counted before inversion and
is amplified by $1/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. No bound for the regularized-operator
difference follows from $\|A-A_h\|\le\eta$ alone.

For a sequence of discretizations and outputs, if $\lambda_j\to0$,
$$\frac{\delta_j+\eta_j\|x^\dagger\|}{\sqrt{\lambda_j}}\to0,\qquad \|(R_{\lambda_j}-R_{\lambda_j,h_j})y_{h_j,\delta_j}\|\to0,\qquad \frac{\|r_{h_j,h_j}\|}{\lambda_j}\to0,$$
then $\widetilde x_{h_j}\to x^\dagger$. If a certified residual evaluation
satisfies $\|r_{h,h}-\widehat r_{h,h}\|\le\rho_{h,h}$, its term may be
bounded by $(\|\widehat r_{h,h}\|+\rho_{h,h})/\lambda$.
